title: test(showcase): bring the teardown-race and approval-resume test files under the 10 s budget
body:
Fixes #23185
Clause-②: no

Brings both `@objectstack/example-showcase` rows of #23185 under the 10 s per-file budget. **This PR closes both rows:**

| file | card reading (slowest of 20 hourly runs) | before, this container | after, this container |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `test/vitest-console-teardown-race.test.ts` | 20.8 s (`38335967790`) | 6.34 s | 2.2–2.5 s idle (5 runs), 2.2–3.2 s beside four concurrent vitest loops (10 runs), 2.95 s inside the full package suite |
| `test/approval-resume-relation-expand.test.ts` | 10.2 s (`38202645321`) | 7.30 s | 2.2–2.3 s idle (3 runs), 2.1–2.5 s beside four concurrent vitest loops (5 runs), 2.55 s inside the full package suite |

"File wall" is the vitest JSON reporter's per-file `endTime - startTime`, the same module duration the refresh lane reads; module loading is outside it. Before is at the base `afbf960c26` and after is at this branch, both on the same 4-vCPU container under the shared verify lock. No timeout was raised, nothing was deleted, and nothing moved to another project. Pin, per the card: the next refresh PR's list no longer names either file.

The fix replaces clocks with sync points. Where the time went, per file:

## `vitest-console-teardown-race.test.ts`: from a race with a retry budget to two ordering facts

**Where the time went.** Each leg spawns a real child vitest, about 1 s each. The ablation leg retried up to 8 times until the teardown race happened to open, and the guarded leg repeated 4 times. On a loaded runner the race rarely opens, so a run paid all 12 children. That is the 20.8 s.

**What was measured on the way.** The race has two windows, both inside vitest, and a green run exits 1 only when both open:

1. In the worker, a console RPC must still be unacknowledged when teardown's `$rejectPendingCalls` sweep runs.
2. In the main process, the worker sends its unhandled-rejection report after it reports the file finished. vitest reads its unhandled errors for the exit code as soon as the pool settles, so a report that arrives after that read is recorded but never graded.

Instrumented traces of the child's main process showed the second window: in the non-reproducing runs the rejection did happen, and its `catchError` landed after `onTestRunEnd`.

**The change.** Both legs now run their child with a harness reporter, `test/fixtures/late-console-teardown/hold-console-acks.reporter.ts`:

- **Window 1 is held open.** vitest's main process answers a console RPC only after every reporter's `onUserConsoleLog` settles. The reporter acknowledges log N only when log N+1 arrives, so the newest console RPC is always unacknowledged, and the sweep always finds one pending. This depends on ordering, not on load. The reporter docblock carries the full argument.
- **Window 2 is read, not raced.** At main-process exit every worker has answered `stop`, after sending its rejection report on the same ordered channel. So the reporter's verdict file records `delivered` (every teardown rejection the main process received) beside `graded` (the ones vitest's exit code saw). The path comes in through vitest's own `--outputFile.holdConsoleAcks=...` option.

As a result, each leg runs once. The ablation grades on `delivered`, and when `graded` is non-zero it also requires a non-zero exit with the error printed. The guarded leg requires `delivered == 0` and exit 0. The skip path and its retry budget are gone: with the hold in place, a premise-intact ablation that delivers nothing is a broken instrument and fails as one. The premise probe gains a sixth marker for the one link the hold adds: the `cli-api` chunk's console RPC handler awaiting the reporters. `PREMISE CONTROL` gains the matching mutation case.

The fixture's first `tick()` now runs synchronously inside its test, so a console RPC exists before teardown takes its `rpcDone()` snapshot. That makes the hold's precondition true by construction. `types/node-shim.d.ts` gains only the members the new code imports.

Prototype measurements (one child per attempt, 4 vCPU, under the verify lock):

| arm | teardown rejection | exit 1 |
|:--|--:|--:|
| idle, vitest defaults, no hold | 20/20 | 20/20 |
| idle, ablation config + hold | 40/40 | 40/40 |
| four concurrent vitest loops, defaults, no hold | 4/20 | 4/20 |
| four concurrent vitest loops, ablation config + hold | 40/40 | 32/40 |
| four concurrent vitest loops, app config + hold | 0/10 | 0/10 |
| four concurrent vitest loops, app config + hold, interception re-armed | 20/20 | 19/20 |

The last column is window 2. It is vitest's own race and no reporter hook can close it, which is why the pin grades the defect on the middle column.

## `approval-resume-relation-expand.test.ts`: the stays-quiet watch ends on a settle point

**Where the time went.** The pre-fix reverse check spent 5.2 s waiting out the full `INBOX_WATCH_MS` window on every run, to conclude that nothing arrived. The first case added a fixed `sleep(200)`.

**The change.**

- `inboxStayedQuiet` takes an optional `settled` predicate. It is asked before the verdict read and ends the observation early. `'quiet'` still rests only on a fresh read taken after the observation ended, which is the #10106 contract, and now records `endedBy: 'settled' | 'deadline'`.
- The call site's predicate is `inboxSettled`: the stranded run is `failed`, and every `sys_notification_delivery` row is in a final state (`success`, `dead` or `suppressed`). Any other state, including one added later, keeps the watch open. These two facts are sufficient because the inbox is a materialization of delivery: no producer writes `sys_inbox_message` directly. The call site asserts `endedBy === 'settled'`, so the 5 s cannot come back silently. `INBOX_WATCH_MS` is unchanged and still only shrinkable.
- The `sleep(200)` is gone. `decide()` awaits the resume (`ApprovalService.serviceResume` awaits `automation.resume`), so the run is already terminal when it returns. Measured with a probe: `completed` right after `decide`, with the inbox row still pending in the outbox. That pending row is what `deliveredInbox` already waits for.
- Three new contract cases, deterministic and with no clock: a settled system ends the watch after exactly two reads; a row that lands before settlement is still seen, because the verdict read comes after the settle check; and `inboxSettled` needs both halves, including fail-safe on an unknown delivery state.

## Ablations (one-time proofs, nothing left in the tree)

Every mutation went through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. Each one showed the anchor count going 1 to 0, a changed blob hash, and, on restore, a blob equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. The expected direction was red each time, and red is what was observed. All runs were at `53ed69f184`, before the merge of main, which touched no file of this package.

| ablation | runs | result |
|:--|--:|:--|
| A1: delete `disableConsoleIntercept: true` from `vitest.config.ts` | 5 idle + 5 beside four concurrent vitest loops | **GUARDED red 10/10** (`delivered: 1`) |
| A2: the hold reporter returns `Promise.resolve()` (no hold) | 12 beside four concurrent vitest loops | **ABLATION red 11/12**, each on the "instrument" branch (premise intact, nothing delivered), never a skip |
| control: no mutation | 5 idle + 10 beside four concurrent vitest loops | green 15/15, file wall 2.2–3.2 s |
| B1: the watch's verdict read becomes the pre-settle sample | 1 | **3 contract cases red** |
| B2: the call site settles on `completed` instead of `failed` | 1 | **pre-fix case red** on `endedBy`, after paying the 5 s window (file 7.23 s) |
| B3: `inboxSettled` drops its outbox half | 1 | **"both halves" contract red** |

## Local verification (at `5ea05a3201`, the head of this PR)

- `vitest run` over the whole package (`examples/app-showcase`, `--maxWorkers=2`): 33 files, 412 tests passed, 0 skipped. It ran beside the gate battery, so the box was loaded. The two files read 2.95 s and 2.55 s, and no other showcase file was over 1.8 s.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/example-showcase typecheck`: exit 0. `tsc --listFiles` counts all 5 touched files in the program.
- Gates derived by `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 39 derived, 38 exit 0, 1 NOT MEASURED. The reconciliation (`--ran`, exit codes recorded) reads "39 derived, 38 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN". The NOT MEASURED one is `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`: its self-test passed (93 cases), then it exited 3 with PREREQUISITE NOT MET, because 8 packages outside this package's dependency closure (`studio`, `client-react`, `embedder-openai`, `knowledge-memory`, `knowledge-ragflow`, `organizations`, `service-cluster-redis`, `service-knowledge`) have no `dist/` in this worktree. No package's `dist/` changes in this diff. CI reads it from a full build.
- Extra: `node scripts/check-console-intercept-disarm.mjs` passed (74 packages disarmed). `pnpm check:nul-bytes` passed.
- Lint, as a proven narrowing. ① Population: the five touched files, which the repo's `eslint.config.mjs` lints; all five were reported, none ignored. ② `--format json` reports 5 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings. ③ Invariance: this config never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService`), so this diff cannot move the verdict for any untouched file. The full `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- No changeset: `@objectstack/example-showcase` is `"private": true` and this diff only touches its tests and type shim, so it publishes nothing. Label: `skip-changeset`.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed)

- vitest's window 2 (a teardown rejection reported after the pool settles is recorded but never graded) is upstream behaviour. It is outside our contract and moot behind `disableConsoleIntercept: true`. Carrier: none.
- `examples/app-showcase/vitest.config.ts` and the header of `scripts/check-console-intercept-disarm.mjs` still describe the window as one load-width span inside `rpcDone()`. The measured second window refines that description but does not contradict either file's prescription, so they are left untouched. Carrier: none.
- The `#10106` watch-contract cases still spend about 1.1 s on real sleeps, by design (latency fakes). That is under budget and unchanged here.
